newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian wool prices fall in week.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian wool prices fall in week.

text.p: Australian wool prices dropped further at sales this week in Sydney, Geelong and Fremantle, the Australian Council of Wool Exporters said.
The eastern market indicator fell by 15 cents to 552 cents a kg clean, while the western market indicator decreased by two cents to 532 cents a kg.

A total of 93,308 bales were offered, with a pass-in rate of 14.9 percent, with a considerable quantity withdrawn before sale and actual offerings only 92 percent of the quantity originally rostered for sale.

Adverse fundamentals in the market, particularly in continental Europe, remained basically unchanged with the quantity of wool available for sale exceeding buyers and processors requirements, it said.
In addition, expectations that the Australian dollar would remain above 80 U.S. cents, for the short-term at least, were starting to negatively affect prices, it said.
The larger quantities of similar types on offer in Sydney and Geelong would also have restricted trade competition and prices in the eastern centres, it said.
Wesfarmers Dalgety Ltd described prices as weakening significantly during the week.

Wool International said it sold a provisional 2,544 bales in the week ended Thursday to bring its stockpile to 1,988,686 bales. Forward sales for the December quarter are 184,454 bales and for the March quarter 16,840 bales, WI said.
In the futures market, a total of 252 contracts were traded in the 21 micron contract in the week ended November 28.
Open interest increased by ten contracts to close at 859.
Sales next week are in Newcastle, Adelaide and Launceston with a total of about 91,000 bales on offer.
